title: The Harbor of Bellbird Bay Anew
premise: Gideon Zhou, a widowed single parent running Bellbird Bay's only bookshop, hires a charming stranger, Marisol Vega—a festival coordinator with a family secret tied to the harbor land—to pose as their date at the Zhou family reunion. What begins as a transaction deepens into real love, but Marisol's employer is the developer buying the harborfront, threatening both the bookshop and the memory-soaked pier where Gideon's late husband once proposed. When Marisol's role in the deal surfaces, Gideon must choose between guarding their rebuilt life and trusting someone who stayed after the last train left. In the end, Gideon's inherited ledger of the town's stories becomes the evidence that saves the harbor, the shop, and their chance at a future together.
about_author: Ansel Amberdale is the pen name of a former harbor-town librarian who writes love stories where small businesses and smaller towns carry the weight of big griefs. They live above a bookshop with a rescue dog named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Three years after losing their husband, Gideon measures life in safe increments: school runs, story hour, closing the shop by six. A letter summons them to the Zhou family reunion, where their aunt plans a matchmaking ambush. Gideon, cornered, blurts that they're seeing someone. Emotional beat: the ache of a life built to avoid risk.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Counter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol arrives in Bellbird Bay to scout the harborfront for her employer's development bid, hiding her purpose. Wandering into the bookshop, she's charmed by Gideon and their daughter Wren. When she overhears Gideon's predicament, she impulsively offers to play the date. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of a convenient lie.

chapters.title: Dessert at the Zhou Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion: nosy aunts, Wren's innocent questions, and a fake-relationship story that grows too specific under interrogation. By dessert, Gideon realizes the lie feels like memory of something real, and Marisol forgets she's acting. Emotional beat: the terrifying warmth of pretending until it isn't pretending.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Low Tide
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Walking the pier after the reunion, Marisol asks about the harbor's history; Gideon shares the shop's inherited ledger, a record of every family the bay has held since 1911. Marisol's employer's name appears in her phone; she silences it. Emotional beat: intimacy deepening on ground Marisol knows is condemned.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol's report is due; the development hinges on the pier and the block containing the bookshop. She drafts the memo, then walks the town collecting stories instead, realizing the ledger is the community's inheritance. She delays filing. Emotional beat: corruption of power seen from inside the hand that wields it.

chapters.title: Wren's Question
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Wren, growing attached, asks if Marisol will still be here after the festival. Gideon deflects, then finds a development notice pinned to the pier board and recognizes Marisol's firm. Doubt curdles everything. Emotional beat: the fear that history repeats—that love arrives wearing a cost.

chapters.title: The Unsent Memo
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol's boss arrives, demanding the harbor file by festival's end, dangling the promotion she traded her integrity toward. She burns the honest draft and submits a falsified one protecting the town, knowing discovery means ruin. Emotional beat: choosing a side before being asked.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The truth detonates: the falsified memo surfaces, and Gideon learns Marisol came to buy their whole life out from under them. A public confrontation at the festival lights; Marisol, exposed, misses the last train on purpose. Emotional beat: betrayal, then the raw question of whether love survives being seen whole.

chapters.title: The Ledger Goes Public
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon, furious but fair, reads the ledger aloud at the harbor meeting—generations of names, marriages, returns. The town claims its inheritance; the development board wavers, and the falsified memo buys time. Gideon finds Marisol on the empty platform. Emotional beat: power returned to memory, and a first true apology.

chapters.title: Bellbird Bay, Anew
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, closing with Gideon's. Marisol takes a job restoring the pier's historical registry alongside Gideon's ledger; the bookshop expands into the harborfront's saved corner. Wren asks if Marisol is staying. She is—past the last train, past the festival, for good. Emotional beat: inheritance chosen rather than imposed; love that stays.
